newsitem.title: USA: Merged Ultramar/Shamrock net seen over estimates.
newsitem.headline: Merged Ultramar/Shamrock net seen over estimates.

text.p: Earnings of a combined Ultramar Corp and Diamond Shamrock Inc in 1997 are are expected to exceed the two companies' First Call estimates by roughly seven to eight percent, Chief Financial Officer Pete Smith said Monday.
Speaking on a teleconference with reporters, he said the merger announced earlier Monday is expected to produce 1998 earnings about 30 percent above Street estimates for the two companies.
First Call's consensus estimates for 1997 are $2.64 per share for Ultramar and $2.66 for Diamond Shamrock.
For 1996, the First Call consensus is $1.91 for Ultramar and $1.72 per share for Diamond Shamrock.
Noting the plan to complete the merger by year end, Smith said the merged company would take a charge against 1996 results to reflect expected merger costs of $67 million.

Ultramar now has about 45 million shares outstanding and has proposed issuing 1.02 shares for each of Diamond Shamrock's 32 million outstanding shares, Ultramar chief executive Jean Gaulin told the teleconference.
Smith is now Ultramar's chief financial officer, Diamond Shamrock spokeswoman Catherine Vignolo said.
The position is vacant at Diamond Shamrock, she noted, adding Smith has been designated to fill it in the merged company.
Gaulin said the merger agreement includes a $45 million backout fee to be paid by either company pulling out of the deal.

Asked about the use of Ultramar stock as the basis for the merger, Diamond Shamrock chief executive Roger Hemminghaus described it has "the most convenient merger vehicle," noting they could have used Diamond Shamrock shares or shares of the newly-merged company.

Gaulin said the 1.02 for one exchange ratio is based on the mean of the trading range for the two stocks since Ultramar Inc went public several months ago, adding "the range (between the two) is fairly low."
Hemminghaus cited margin calls and "speculation on press reports" for the runup in Diamond Shamrock's stock last week, but declined to comment on, or even describe, those reports.
Both chief executives said the merger grew out of the companies' exchange of information the past few years under a technology exchange agreement.
This effort was possible because of the lack of direct competition between the two companies, they explained.

Gaulin said the merged company will delay station building plans Ultramar had for California and eastern Canada. The company had planned to spend about $50 million on new stations of three years, he said.
Asked about this statement, he said most of the delays will be in California, adding it will postpone 10 service stations the company had planned to build in eastern Canada.
He said Ultramar is going ahead with plans to build 600 convenience stores in Canada, noting 100 are in place.
